thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — cassini-prod (Private VPC) reporting elevated 502/504s for ingress and intermittent failures for outbound auth calls. Trigger: 5xx spike, pager firing.

sara: I’m on call. paging network oncall @manny and infra @alex. Customer-facing team @customer-success FYI — Cassini is seeing request failures for the dedicated tenant pool.

manny: grabbing logs. initial hypothesis — NLB health flapping + egress token fetch to auth provider (third-party) timing out. seeing timeouts to 34.210.55.101 from natgw metrics.

alex: checking NLB target group health now.

alex: run: ```aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-cassini/abcdef123456```
output: ```{ "TargetHealthDescriptions": [ { "Target": { "Id": "i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g" }, "TargetHealth": { "State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "Target.Timeout" } }, { "Target": { "Id": "i-0b1c2d3e4f5g6h" }, "TargetHealth": { "State": "healthy" } } ] }```

manny: interesting — one backend is flapping. but failed requests are also 20% hitting healthy instances and still 5xxing. suspect downstream auth egress.

jess: customer reports errors on login and model calls timing out around 14:02 UTC. They see DNS responses occasionally high TTL or NXDOMAIN? getting screenshots.

ops-bot: Runbook link added — <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-egress-504|vpc-egress-504 runbook>.

sara: immediate mitigation plan: 1) isolate whether egress block -> allow specific auth IPs on SG, 2) shift ingress weight to standby ALB in secondary AZ/region if NLB instability persists, 3) contact Cassini account manager about mitigation and status. Doing step 1 now.

manny: checking security group outbound rules for tenant pool. current outbound is locked to 0.0.0.0/0 blocked except allowlist to internal services. auth provider IPs not allowed. seeing deny to 34.210.55.0/24.

manny: adding temporary SG egress rule to allow 34.210.55.101:443 from cassini-tg-sg (will expire in 1h). ```aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0abc1234 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 34.210.55.101/32```

ops-bot: Security group change by @manny applied (change-id chg-0f1e2d3c).

alex: rechecking natgw metrics and connection counts. natgw outgoing connections to 34.210.55.101 were spiking and then blackholed when conntrack exhausted. added a small burst NAT instance route as temporary.

manny: also noticed DNS for internal auth host resolves to different IPs, TTL was 300s. running: ```dig +noall +answer auth1.thirdparty.net @10.0.0.2``` -> gave `auth1.thirdparty.net. 300 IN A 34.210.55.101`

dmitri: recommend we also add a fallback DNS weight—point `cassini-api.redwood.internal` to the standby ALB for 10% traffic until NLB stabilizes. I can make the weighted record change in Route53 (private hosted zone).

sara: please proceed @dmitri, make the weight 90/10 favoring primary still but allow some traffic to standby ALB to verify auth path.

dmitri: done. Route53 change: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"cassini-api.internal.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"standby-alb","Weight":10,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.10.5.20"}]}}]}'```

ops-bot: Route53 change submitted (change-id /change/C12345). TTL lowered to 60s.

customer-success: pinged Cassini support contact, they acknowledged and asked for ETA. I told them we're on mitigation and will update within 30m.

manny: after SG egress allow and route shift, auth failures dropped from 28% -> 4% within 5 minutes. NLB target flapping still logged but not causing majority of user-facing errors.

jess: monitoring dashboards show request latency normalizing. errors by region: us-east-1 primary still slightly elevated.

alex: digging into why target went unhealthy — seeing large GC pauses on i-0a1b2c3d, looks like an application memory leak on that instance. I've removed it from the target group and we will cordon it. Scaling policy will spin up a replacement.```aws autoscaling terminate-instance-in-auto-scaling-group --instance-id i-0a1b2c3d --should-decrement-desired-capacity false```

manny: verifying conntrack counts on NAT: ```sudo conntrack -S | grep entries``` -> temporarily high, dropped after NAT instance route added. We'll follow up to increase conntrack table on NAT fleet.

sara: current status: ingress 90% healthy, auth egress failures down to baseline, NLB has one bad backend removed, DNS weighted fallback active 10%. customer notified.

dmitri: follow-ups: 1) postmortem to identify why SG egress allowlist didn't include thirdparty auth IPs for this tenant, 2) add monitoring alert for auth egress failures per-tenant, 3) increase conntrack on NAT fleet and revisit autoscaling for NAT throughput.

jess: customer response: appreciate fast mitigation, will want a writeup and SLA credit assessment. I told them we'll produce a postmortem and follow-up by EOD.

ops-bot: Scheduling postmortem meeting — draft created and assigned to @sara.

sara: thanks team. leaving a note for SRE rotation: if NLB target flapping reappears, immediate steps = 1) remove affected instance from target group, 2) verify SG egress to auth provider, 3) shift DNS weight to standby, 4) escalate to platform when >15% global errors.

manny: acknowledging handoff to next oncall @alex + @dmitri for follow-up.

sara: clearing page — incident mitigated. will own postmortem and timeline. :white_check_mark:
